title: Europe and Central Asia’s jobs problem is a productivity and firm-capability problem, not simply a shortage of capital or workers
source_unit: World Bank, TIDES of Change: Igniting Productivity Growth in Europe and Central Asia
geography: Europe and Central Asia; 16-country, multi-sector firm-level evidence spanning 2008–2023

denominator.unit: harmonized firm-level observations assembled from national statistical offices, tax authorities and complementary sources across 16 countries and multiple sectors

productivity_to_jobs.unit: additional jobs that a 10% increase in productivity could add in the region

post_2008_productivity_gap.unit: percent higher regional GDP that might have resulted if post-2008 productivity growth had matched its pre-financial-crisis pace

productivity_slowdown.value: The region’s post-global-financial-crisis growth slowdown was almost entirely driven by slower productivity

observations.method: World Bank analysis using harmonized firm-level data and regional productivity, employment and growth comparisons.
observations.uncertainty: The job and GDP figures are model-based estimates or counterfactuals, not guaranteed outcomes; the report’s firm data may not capture all informal activity or household-level constraints.
observations.subgroup: Firms, workers and sectors across 16 Europe and Central Asia countries.
observations.counterinterpretation: Productivity gains can raise jobs and wages when demand, competition and distributional institutions transmit gains; otherwise they may concentrate returns among high-productivity firms and capital owners.

observations.period: 2025; firm capability, trade and value-chain integration

denominator.unit: ECA firms and countries analyzed in the World Bank TIDES report; subgroup denominators vary by measure

exporter_productivity.value: Exporters are the most productive firms and, although a small minority, disproportionately contribute to jobs, investment and value added

trade_untapped_potential.unit: percent less trade on average than the region could achieve

nearshoring_opportunity.value: Closer-to-home and more resilient value chains create an opportunity if domestic firms can strengthen capabilities and engage with multinational firms

observations.method: Firm-level productivity and trade analysis combined with regional value-chain and foreign-investment assessment.
observations.uncertainty: The trade gap is an estimate relative to modeled potential and does not ensure that expanded trade produces broad-based wages, local ownership or resilient household outcomes.
observations.subgroup: Exporting and domestic firms, multinational firms and workers across ECA countries.
observations.counterinterpretation: Export concentration can improve aggregate productivity while increasing regional or sectoral inequality if smaller firms, workers and lagging places cannot enter the value chain.

observations.period: 2025; reform bundle for productivity and job quality

denominator.unit: World Bank regional policy analysis; no single respondent or firm denominator for the reform bundle

tides_bundle.value: Trade, investment, digitalization, efficiency and skills are identified as mutually reinforcing reform priorities

firm_constraints.value: Weak firm capabilities, incomplete global-market integration, market distortions and persistent less-efficient state-owned enterprises constrain productivity

public_governance.value: Governments are urged to mainstream productivity into plans and budgets, enable competition, ensure transparent procurement and measure reform progress

skills_and_technology.value: Productivity rises when firms can access technology and finance and workers can acquire skills to adopt and adapt

observations.method: Comparative economic analysis and policy synthesis from firm-level and country-level evidence.
observations.uncertainty: The report identifies a reform bundle but does not establish that all components have equal marginal effects or that implementation is politically feasible in every country.
observations.subgroup: Governments, firms, workers, investors and education/training systems in ECA.
observations.counterinterpretation: Productivity reform without worker voice, social protection and regional redistribution can intensify the same legitimacy and middle-class anxieties documented in the World Bank’s qualitative work.

denominator.unit: ECA labor-market and demographic projections; country-group denominators vary

employment_growth.unit: percent increase in ECA employment over the last 15 years

services_share.value: Services now account for more than half of jobs in the region

low_skill_opportunity.value: Most recent opportunities have been relatively low-skilled jobs with limited earning potential

working_age_decline.unit: projected decrease in the working-age population over the coming decades, concentrated in Eastern and Central Europe and the Western Balkans

regional_divergence.value: Central Asia and Türkiye are projected to see working-age population growth, creating a different labor-market pressure

observations.method: World Bank regional labor-market, demographic and sector-composition analysis.
observations.uncertainty: Projections depend on fertility, migration, health, retirement, participation and policy assumptions; employment growth does not by itself indicate rising job quality or household security.
observations.subgroup: Workers, youth, women and older people across different ECA demographic subregions.
observations.counterinterpretation: Population decline can raise worker bargaining power in some sectors, while population growth can create opportunity if job creation and skills investment keep pace.

World Bank ECA Economic Update context on job quality, demographics, infrastructure and skills.

boundary: This record adds a supply-side mobility mechanism: broad job and wage improvement depends on productivity, firm capability, competition, technology access, trade integration and skills—not merely adding capital or workers. It is regional macroeconomic and firm-level analysis with model-based estimates, not a household survey, worker-panel dataset or guarantee that productivity gains will be evenly distributed.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The official World Bank TIDES press release, publication context, report PDF and ECA Economic Update press release were retrieved and reviewed for productivity, jobs, trade, firm capability, reform priorities, job quality and demographic transition; the report PDF was hashed.
